content: The image shows a corn field with visibly stunted plants — some plants are significantly shorter than the surrounding taller plants, with what appears to be shortened internodes. The leaves look somewhat lighter/yellowish-green. No obvious leaf spots, pustules, or ear rot visible. This stunting pattern narrows candidates to: Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus, or Maize_chlorotic_dwarf_virus.

The Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma reference shows advanced-stage disease with reddish-purple discoloration and dried-out tissue — quite different from the test image which shows actively growing but noticeably stunted green plants.

Key observations from test image:
- Plants in field center/foreground are visibly much shorter than surrounding plants
- Shortened internodes apparent
- Plants still green (no reddish-purple coloration visible)
- No mosaic pattern, no pustules, no spots, no ear rot

The stunting with shortened internodes matches **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma** (plants "often only 5 feet tall with very short internodes") — the reddish-purple coloring described is an age-dependent symptom that may not be present at this growth stage. The visual of distinctly shorter plants scattered among taller normal plants is the hallmark field symptom.
